pricesPage.title: What does a case management system cost?
pricesPage.description: There is no fixed price list. The price follows scope: which case types you need, which national components the solution must talk to, and whether you are buying development, operations, or both.
pricesPage.whyTitle: Why we do not publish a price list
pricesPage.whyBody: A case management system for three case types and one for a directorate with dozens of integrations are not the same delivery. Contract form, archive requirements, and whether the solution is shared or standalone all change both the work and the risk. A table of kroner would either be too generic to use, or so specific that it only described one project.
pricesPage.driversLead: These are the items that actually change an estimate for a Norwegian public-sector line-of-business system. We price them after discovery, not as a finished package.

cases.title: Case types
cases.body: How many case types, which steps from submission to decision, and whether the flow is the same or different per type.

integrations.title: National shared components
integrations.body: Altinn, ID-porten, Maskinporten, the Population Register, the Register of Legal Entities, KS Fiks and Noark. Access, test environments and error handling take more time than the API call itself.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.body: WCAG 2.2 AA is a requirement for public services. It is cheaper to build in than to fix after the solution is in production.

archive.title: Archiving
archive.body: Noark integration belongs in the data model from the start. Reconstructing journal entries afterwards becomes expensive and fragile.

migration.title: Data migration
migration.body: Moving cases, documents and history from an existing system is its own piece of work, with its own assumptions.

tenancy.title: Multi-tenant or dedicated install
tenancy.body: A shared platform and a dedicated install have different operating cost, isolation and upgrade rhythm.

contract.title: SSA-S or SSA-L
contract.body: Time-and-materials development and a running service agreement price risk differently. The choice belongs to the procurement, not to a finished package.

operations.title: Operations after launch
operations.body: Most of the cost in a line-of-business system's life comes after go-live. Updates, monitoring and further development are agreed separately.

pricesPage.scopeTitle: What is included, and what is priced separately

included.title: Typically included
included.body: Discovery with stated assumptions, architecture and data model, development in increments, testing and go-live, and documentation you can take over.

separate.title: Priced separately
separate.body: Integrations with shared components you do not already have an agreement for, data migration, adapting an existing line-of-business system, and a maintenance agreement after launch.

transparensPage.description: We are direct about how we run what we build: the uptime and SLA commitments we take on, how security is built into the work, and who to contact if something breaks.

sla.title: Uptime and SLA agreements
sla.description: Uptime and SLA targets are agreed per project and set out in the operations agreement. Thresholds and follow-up are matched to how critical the solution is.

security.title: Operations and security
security.description: We are ISO 27001 certified. Operations and security are part of the delivery from day one — operability and availability are design decisions we make with you, not an afterthought.

incidents.title: Incidents and status
incidents.description: If you experience downtime or a deviation from the agreed SLA, contact us directly. We report status and follow-up through the channel set out in your operations agreement.
